rule: The github-reviewer runs a read-only bump-type version check after its fix commit and before its push, goes on to the push only when the check exits 0 with a version_check of match, unreadable or undetermined, stops blocked on any other result, and never edits a version file
description: `plugin/agents/github-reviewer.md` step 7 is the canonical source for the reviewer's version check. When the project's `CLAUDE.md` names version files, the reviewer invokes `hivemind:bump-type` through the Skill tool once, with the remote-tracking base `origin/<allowlist-validated-base>`, its two Bump Trigger judgments over the whole branch, and those files. The check is load-bearing because a review fix can change runtime behavior on a branch whose version file was never raised, and the push is the last point before that commit reaches the PR. The routing is a positive allowlist with a default stop: the check passes only on exit 0 with a `version_check` of `match`, `unreadable` or `undetermined` (the ADR-0040 D3 recorded pass on `unreadable` and `undetermined` results), and every other result stops, so a mismatch under any verdict, a failed check, a missing, unknown or malformed `version_check` and any value the check adds later all stop without being listed. The source pin is ONE span that starts at the tail of the commit SHA gate sentence and carries the condition (CLAUDE.md names version files), the invocation through the Skill tool by skill name, the base, the two judgments with their governance citation, the whole-branch scope and the version files, so deleting the condition, swapping the Skill invocation for another form, dropping the base, the judgments or the files, or moving the clause away from the commit gate tail turns the suite red. A consumer pin in the same file carries the pass rule as ONE span that starts at the tail of the invocation sentence (`and those files.`): the exit 0 condition, `only`, the three passing values and the default stop with its `blocker_reason` naming any `expected_version`, so adding, dropping or swapping a value, dropping the exit 0 condition or `only`, inverting the stop, dropping `expected_version`, or inserting text after `and those files.` turns the suite red. A second consumer pin carries, as ONE span, the relay of the check's output when no `expected_version` is present, the never-bump clause (never edit a version file) and the start of the existing Unsafe Git State check and push sentence, so deleting or rewording the relay or the never-bump clause, or separating them from the push sentence, turns the suite red. What these pins honestly guarantee is exactly that these three word sequences exist in this one named file; they claim nothing about meaning and nothing about what the reviewer actually runs. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) the pins check the order of the text, the check clause sitting between the commit gate and the push sentence, not the order in which the reviewer acts, so a reviewer that pushes before it checks is invisible; (2) a presence pin cannot assert body-prose absence, so a reviewer-side version bump added elsewhere in the file, a pass for another result added elsewhere in the file, or surrounding prose that offers one as an alternative to stopping, stays green; (3) the pins are whole-file presence pins, not section-scoped, though the anchoring on the commit gate tail and the push sentence holds them inside step 7 while those sentences stay there; (4) the bump-type verdict, `version_check` and `expected_version` semantics, including which `version_check` values exist and when `expected_version` is present, are owned by `plugin/skills/bump-type/SKILL.md` and its engine and are not pinned here; (5) the absence of a check when `CLAUDE.md` names no version file is carried only by the pinned condition and by the allowlist naming the check's own result, not by any separate clause.

source.pattern: `blocker_reason: input outside the safe identifier allowlist`. When `CLAUDE.md` names version files, invoke `hivemind:bump-type` (Skill tool) once with base `origin/<allowlist-validated-base>`, your two judgments per `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/versioning.md` (Bump Trigger) over the whole branch, and those files.

consumers.pattern: and those files. The check passes only on exit 0 with a `version_check` of `match`, `unreadable` or `undetermined`; any other result returns `blocked`, `blocker_reason` naming any `expected_version`,
`expected_version`, else relaying the check's output. Never edit a version file. Then verify git state is safe per `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/definitions.md` (Unsafe Git State) and push once
